text:
jason: Heads-up — noticed persistent prefix cache hit-rate gap between regions after the kernel-selector rollout. us-west hit ~62% on the test load, eu-west only ~18%. p95 token latency in eu jumped ~210ms.
li: Yikes. Is this steady across traffic or a cold-start artifact?
sasha: Are we seeing replication lag or key mismatch?
jason: Both. Replication lag sits at 3–7s during peak (we're seeing bursts). Also profiling shows different KV key serialization bytes after the new kernel binary — alignment/padding changed for some model variants, so identical prompts map to different keys.
li: Can you paste the problematic key derivation?
jason: Sure — simplified version from runtime:
```
def cache_key(model_id, seq_hash, prompt_norm):
    # before: compact serialization + little-endian ints
    return sha256(f"{model_id}:{seq_hash}:{prompt_norm}").hexdigest()
    
# after kernel-selector build we ship: struct.pack('=I', seq_len) -> native-endian on some hosts
```
li: Ah — native-endian packing on some regions would explain mismatches without replication ever touching it.
maya: So keys differ at source, not a replication bug. That fits the hit split. What about warmup? eu region seems colder overall.
andrew: Our customer-facing SLOs start seeing errors when eu p95 creeps up. Any short-term mitigations?
sasha: Short-term: change routing policy to prefer-warm (route to region with higher local prefix-hit) and allow cross-region fallback only if latency < X ms. Also we can enable SWR (stale-while-revalidate) for 5s to avoid hard misses.
li: For the serialization issue we can either revert the kernel-selector change or normalize key serialization at runtime (force network/little-endian canonicalization). Normalization is safer.
jason: Agree. I'll open a quickfix PR to canonicalize key bytes before hashing. That should immediately unify keys across regions.
deploy-bot: canary deploy of runtime/kv-normalize started on eu-west at 18:12 UTC (canary=10%).
li: Parallel work: add a small deterministic prompt-normalizer to reduce entropy from trailing whitespace/zero-width chars — that improved hit-rate locally by ~6%.
jason: Profiling numbers post-fix are promising in sim: local hit rises from 18% -> ~58% for eu on replayed traffic. p95 token latency drops ~180ms. We'll need to monitor for false positives.
maya: Does enabling prefer-warm routing risk overloading us-west? We should rate-limit cross-region fallback.
sasha: Plan: prefer-warm routing + token-budgeted fallbacks (max 10% of QPS allowed cross-region) + prefetch warmups during deploys for eu (background prefetch of top 1k prefixes).
andrew: Can we precompute top prefixes per customer and push to cold regions during off-peak? That'd help PLG usage.
li: Yes — we have the tooling to extract top-k prefixes per tenant. We'll add TTL of 600s and a jittered prefetch schedule.
jason: Note: another regression traced to kernel selector was slight change in KV eviction ordering under high memory pressure. That amplified misses during spikes. We'll pin eviction policy in the hotfix.
maya: Action items?
jason: 1) li: PR to canonicalize key bytes + add small normalizer (ETA 2h). 2) sasha: rollout prefer-warm routing + token-budgeted fallback (ETA next deploy). 3) li & ops: prefetch job for top-k prefixes with TTL 600s (ETA tomorrow morning). 4) jason: monitor dashboard cards for eu hit-rate, cross-region QPS, replication lag (alert if eu hit < 40% or replication lag > 5s).
sasha: I'll add alerts and a temporary playbook snippet.
andrew: Good. Keep comms to #incidents if SLOs start tripping.
li: Quick note — adding a unit test for key canonicalization and a replay test that compares hashes across host endian combos.
jason: Will post PR and perf replay results here when completed. Thanks all :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary of runtime/kv-normalize finished: success. metrics: eu hit-rate +35 pp in canary cohort.
jason: Rolling to 100% now. Monitoring...
maya: Thanks — let's sync in 30m for final verification.
